methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective/prospective registry study of 95 mPDAC patients from 13 centers (SlovPac). Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression appropriately applied. Limitations: small sample size, non-standardized data collection across sites, missing detailed baseline data on comorbidities/frailty, selection bias in third-line eligibility, performance status effect not rigorously assessed.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Observational cohort examining prognostic biomarkers in third-line mPDAC. Identifies PNI and GPS as prognostic factors but limited mechanistic insight. Findings potentially useful for patient selection but no intervention or treatment comparison.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods describe data source (SlovPac registry), inclusion criteria, biomarker calculations, statistical analysis. Results present baseline characteristics and survival stratified by biomarkers. Limited detail on registry data quality, standardization across 13 centers. Data availability not discussed.

novelty_literature.justification: Confirms known prognostic biomarkers (PNI, GPS) in metastatic PDAC context. Application to third-line treatment population is incremental. No novel mechanism identified. Findings align with prior literature on nutritional/inflammatory markers.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear Methods and Results sections with appropriate Kaplan-Meier curves. Discussion contextualizes findings within prior studies and compares regimens. Organization adequate but some sections repetitive. Tables effectively present subgroup analyses.

key_strengths: Multicenter registry data (13 sites) provides diverse patient population representation
Identifies PNI >40.5 and GPS 0 as independent prognostic factors for OS/PFS in third-line setting
Appropriate statistical methods (Kaplan-Meier, multivariate Cox) for survival analysis
key_concerns: Small sample size (95 patients) limits power to detect moderate effects and assess interaction/confounding
Non-standardized data collection across 13 centers introduces measurement error; no quality control assessment
Missing critical baseline data (comorbidities, frailty) limit confounder adjustment
Limited novelty: confirms known prognostic factors; no new insights into third-line treatment efficacy or mechanisms
chief_reviewer.rationale: Small retrospective registry study confirming nutritional/inflammatory markers as prognostic in third-line mPDAC. Limited novelty and sample size preclude strong inference. Multicenter nature provides some generalizability but non-standardized data collection undermines quality. Tier 4 appropriate for incremental confirmatory finding.
